entities.summary: Agrinio is the largest city and municipality of the Aetolia-Acarnania regional unit of Greece, as well as the second largest city in Western Greece after Patras. It is the economic center of Aetolia-Acarnania, although its capital is the town of Mesolonghi. The settlement dates back to ancient times. Ancient Agrinion was 3 kilometres northeast of the present city; some walls and foundations of which have been excavated. In medieval times and until 1836, the city was known as Vrachori (Βραχώρι). According to the 2021 census, the municipality of Agrinio has a population of 89,691, of whom 50,690 live within the city limits of Agrinio.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the economic center of Aetolia-Acarnania, Agrinio played a significant role in regional trade and commerce during ancient times. Its population has grown to 89,691, making it an important urban hub in modern Greece.
